title: chore: prune the Serena memory store — archive the handoffs of finished tasks out of list_memories, and merge duplicate gotcha memories
description:
Requested by the human on 2026-10-30 after a governor audit of Serena usage, covering Serena's own logs for 10-27 to 10-30 and .serena/memories.

The audit:
- .serena/memories holds 758 files (~2 MB).
- 349 are task handoffs (task-task-<id>-handoff). 304 of them belong to tasks that are already DONE (203) or ARCHIVED (101); only 45 belong to live tasks.
- 277 are gotcha-* files, which likely overlap heavily. docs/MEMORY.md says to prefer edit_memory over near-duplicates, but nothing enforces it.
- One list_memories call now returns about 36 KB of names (~9k tokens), mostly dead handoffs.

Serena 1.6.2 (WSL, ~/.local/bin/serena) supports `ignored_memory_patterns` in .serena/project.yml. These are regexes, fullmatched against the memory name, and a match is excluded from listing, reading and writing (serena/memories/memory_manager.py). So archived files can be kept on disk but hidden from the tools.

Scope:
1. Move every task-*-handoff memory whose task is DONE or ARCHIVED on the board (read status through moe tools, never by hand-editing .moe) into .serena/memories/_archive/, keeping its name. Then add the pattern `_archive/.*` to .serena/project.yml ignored_memory_patterns. Never move the handoff of a task in PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL, WORKING, REVIEW or BLOCKED.
2. Merge duplicate or near-duplicate gotcha-* (and decision-*) memories. Fold each group into one file named per docs/MEMORY.md, keeping every distinct fact, and archive the merged-away files the same way. Re-point any `mem:<name>` reference you find in the task plans you touch.

Safety: .serena/ is untracked but NOT gitignored, and no commit has ever touched .serena/memories. A landing with attribution.undeclared 'solo' could sweep hundreds of moved files into git. Declare nothing under .serena, and confirm after landing that `git log --oneline -- .serena` is still empty. Whether .serena/memories should be gitignored or added to attribution.exclude is a human call, so ask; don't decide it.
definitionOfDone: Every task-*-handoff memory whose task is DONE or ARCHIVED is in .serena/memories/_archive/, and no live task's handoff moved. The completion summary gives both counts (before and after) and the list of moved names.

.serena/project.yml ignored_memory_patterns contains `_archive/.*`. A fresh Serena session's list_memories (or an equivalent MemoryManager check) shows none of the archived names, and the listing is measurably smaller (state the before and after size).

Duplicate gotcha-*/decision-* groups are merged into single files with no distinct fact dropped, each merge listed as 'kept <name> <- merged <names>'. No path under .serena is committed: `git log --oneline -- .serena` is still empty after the landing.

implementationPlan.description:
BASELINE AND SELECTION. Read-only; nothing moves in this step.

(1) Before-listing: run the installed Serena's own lister in a fresh process with the CURRENT config:
`~/.local/share/uv/tools/serena-agent/bin/python -c "import yaml; from serena.memories.memory_manager import MemoryManager as M; p=yaml.safe_load(open('.serena/project.yml')).get('ignored_memory_patterns') or []; n=M('.serena', ignored_memory_patterns=p).list_project_memories().get_full_list(); print(len(n), len(' '.join(n)))"`
Record the count and chars. That is the 'before' for DoD 2; the audit measured about 36 KB.

(2) Board status, through moe tools only, never by editing .moe:
- DONE ids: moe.list_tasks {status:['DONE'], limit:500}, paging with offset until returned < limit;
- ARCHIVED ids: moe.list_tasks {status:['ARCHIVED'], includeArchived:true}, paged the same way;
- live ids: PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL, WORKING, REVIEW, BLOCKED and BACKLOG.

(3) Selection over TOP-LEVEL files of .serena/memories only. The daemon/ and jetbrains/ topic subdirs are never touched. Select names that fullmatch `task-(task-[0-9a-f]{32})-(qa-)?handoff\.md` and whose id is DONE or ARCHIVED. 'task-*-handoff' includes the -qa-handoff files.
- A live id is never selected.
- An id that is not on the board at all (a deleted task) stays put and is only counted.
- Write the move list and the counts (selected, live kept, unknown kept) to a scratch file outside the repo.

Error handling: a failed list_tasks page, or a name that matches neither set, stops the step. Never guess a status.

Board paged through Moe: 156 DONE, 348 ARCHIVED, 58 live; selection/counts at /tmp/moe-memory-prune-78ba155c/selection.json. Shared dirty paths untouched; only read-only git log/status used. No source fixes or tests needed (memory maintenance).

implementationPlan.description:
ARCHIVE AND HIDE. Use one small Python script (in scratch, outside the repo). Never use git, and never use Serena rename_memory 300 times.

(1) Create .serena/memories/_archive/. For each selected file, os.rename it to _archive/<same basename>.
- If the destination exists, skip that file and report it. Never overwrite.
- After the loop, assert that every selected name is now in _archive/ and that no live-id handoff moved.

(2) Edit .serena/project.yml by replacing exactly the line `ignored_memory_patterns: []` with:
```
ignored_memory_patterns:
- _archive/.*
```
Every other byte stays unchanged. Re-load the file with yaml.safe_load and assert that the list equals ['_archive/.*'] and that the other keys are unchanged.

Serena fullmatches the pattern against the memory name ('_archive/<name>'). A match is excluded from list, read and write, and the raw file remains readable with the Read tool. Running Serena servers keep their old config until restart, so measure with a fresh process.

The wrappers' pre-flight memory preload already scans only the top level (`find -maxdepth 1` in sh, non-recursive Get-ChildItem in ps1), so archived names drop out of <inbox> automatically.

Error handling: on any assert failure, print the offending names and stop. Fix the move by hand with os.rename back before retrying.

implementationPlan.description:
VERIFY, once and fresh. QA re-runs the same command after the landing. It reads .moe/tasks read-only:
```
cd /mnt/d/projexts/moes && test -z "$(git log --oneline -- .serena)" && ~/.local/share/uv/tools/serena-agent/bin/python - <<'PY'
import glob, json, os, re, sys, yaml
from serena.memories.memory_manager import MemoryManager
pats = yaml.safe_load(open('.serena/project.yml', encoding='utf-8')).get('ignored_memory_patterns') or []
assert '_archive/.*' in pats, pats
names = MemoryManager('.serena', ignored_memory_patterns=pats).list_project_memories().get_full_list()
assert not [n for n in names if n.startswith('_archive/')]
arch = glob.glob('.serena/memories/_archive/task-task-*handoff.md')
bad = []
for f in arch:
    m = re.fullmatch(r'task-(task-[0-9a-f]{32})-(?:qa-)?handoff\.md', os.path.basename(f))
    p = '.moe/tasks/%s.json' % m.group(1) if m else ''
    st = json.load(open(p, encoding='utf-8')).get('status') if p and os.path.exists(p) else None
    if st not in ('DONE', 'ARCHIVED'): bad.append((os.path.basename(f), st))
print('listed=%d chars=%d archived_handoffs=%d bad=%s' % (len(names), len(' '.join(names)), len(arch), bad))
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
PY
```
It must exit 0, and its listed/chars give the 'after' for DoD 2 against step 1's 'before'. Its fresh output is the complete_task verification evidence.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Serena delete_memory: rejected. Moving into _archive/ plus ignored_memory_patterns keeps history readable on disk.
- Calling rename_memory per file: rejected. There are about 300 files, and renaming into an ignored name is refused once the pattern exists.
- Reading every gotcha file to find duplicates: rejected for token cost. Name-similarity clusters (14 groups, 43 files when checked at planning) plus seeded topic groups bound the reads.
- Splitting archive and merge into two tasks: rejected, because the human-owned DoD carries both.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: At planning there were 780 top-level memory files: 359 handoffs (51 of them qa-handoffs), 285 gotcha-* and 94 decision-*, in 3.6 MB. Both wrappers DENY untracked .serena/** at landing, so the commit risk the description names is already blocked; the verification still asserts it. The pre-flight <inbox> memory names come from a top-level disk scan, so archived handoffs disappear from it with no wrapper change.
planningNotes.risks:
- Running Serena servers keep the old (empty) ignore list until restart, so their list_memories shows the _archive/ names until then. Measure with a fresh process.
- Live memories that cite archived handoffs as mem:<name> become unreadable through read_memory (read_file still works). Count them in the summary and do not rewrite them.
- A task reopened from DONE later would find its handoff archived. That is rare and recoverable by moving the file back.
